title_en: Ninety-Nine Years of Worry and One Year of Joy
source_file: 40九十九年烦恼和一年快乐（7-10岁）.pptx
full_text_zh:
[P1] 九十九年烦恼和一年快乐

[P2] 老犀牛爷爷活了九十九岁了。
他糊里糊涂地过了九十九个年头。
他一辈子都在找东西，找自己的
东西，找自己不知道放在哪里的东西。

大家知道，老犀牛爷爷从他还是
娃娃的时候开始，记性就很差，他每天
都要在找东西中花掉很多时间。

比如，上学了——他不知道书包
放在哪儿；上课了——翻遍书包也找
不到铅笔；回家了——他摸遍所有的
口袋无法找到开门的钥匙；在家做作业——他又发
现课本放在
教室里了……

总之，他很糊
涂！

062
063

[P3] 到老了，他还是这样。每天清晨，他要光着脚找鞋，然后端着茶缸去找牙刷，找到牙刷后再去找牙膏，还没等到洗脸，已经花去整整两个小时了。

有人帮犀牛爷爷算了一笔账，他在九十九年中，睡觉花了三十三年——这和大家一样。剩下的六十六年，他大概有

六十个年头是在找东西——找自己的东西。只有六个年头是在干他应该干的事情。

这话一点也不夸张，老犀牛爷爷自己也承认，他一辈子都在为这苦恼。小朋友们也许有这种体会吧，一直在找东西的人，心情是不会愉快的。老犀牛爷爷就因为找东西找得太多了，神经太紧张，得了心脏病和高血压。

[P4] 就在老犀牛爷爷过了九十九岁生日后，他家旁边搬来了一位新邻居，这是一只小浣熊。

浣熊小弟非常爱干净。老犀牛爷爷是在溪边认识他的，小浣熊常在溪边洗东西。手绢啦，汗衫啦，还有吃的东西，他样样都要洗。

浣熊的家里也干净极了，到处一尘不染，东西都井井有条，房间里没有一件乱放的东西，布置得就像商店的大橱窗一样，看上去又漂亮，又舒服。

[P5] 不久,小浣熊来到老犀牛爷爷家
里做客。一走进门,他吓了一跳:他简直就像到了杂货仓库,到处是乱七八糟的东西,连脚都没处放。老犀牛爷爷想倒茶给客人喝,可是怎么也找不到茶杯。

小浣熊下定决心,要帮助老犀牛爷爷整理好屋子。他花了整整三天的时间,把屋子里一半没有用的东西扔了出去,剩下的一半每一件都洗了洗,洗得溪水都发黑了。

[P6] 老犀牛爷爷简直认不出自己的房子了，它是那么宽敞，那么明亮。他只有在剧场里看戏的时候，才看到过那么好看的房子。

老犀牛爷爷脱下皮靴，刚想钻到橱柜底下去找拖鞋，小浣熊说：“不！拖鞋在床下。”老犀牛第一次顺手就拿到了拖鞋。他高兴极了，笑得满脸起了皱纹。

天已经很晚了，老犀牛爷爷在干净暖和的床上睡下了。

[P7] 第二天一早，当他翻身坐起来时，
想起了小浣熊昨天教他的歌：
“拖鞋、皮靴床底下，
窗台上面有牙刷。
面盆就在水池边，
花花毛巾墙角挂。
用完东西别乱放，
请把它们送回家。”

平常两个小时也完不成的事情，
今天十分钟就完成了，老犀牛爷爷惊奇极了。

早上的空气多么好，老犀牛爷爷
想去河边散步。以往他早上是没
有时间散步的。他想钻到床底下去
找鞋、帽和外套。突然，他想起了：
“门后挂着，围巾和帽。
柜里藏着，衣服外套。
请你回家，照样放好。”

[P8] 五分钟后，老犀牛爷爷就穿戴好出门了。走在小河边，他向遇到的所有朋友问好，他的心情好极了。朋友们也很高兴，他们第一次看到老犀牛爷爷穿得整整齐齐，一大清早出来散步了。

不用说，从那以后，老犀牛爷爷的生活也变得井然有序了，他再也不用整天找东西，他的心脏病、高血压也好了。他整天笑容满面。

很不幸，就在过了一百岁生日后，老犀牛爷爷患了重感冒，又得了肺炎，一病不起了。老犀牛爷爷知道自己病没法治了，因为他年龄太大了。

[P9] 他对来探望他的伙伴们说：“我很愉快，我活了一百岁，可是过了九十九年烦恼的日子。多亏小浣熊的帮助，我这一年生活得真快活，我快活极了！但愿大家都能像我一样，不像小浣熊一样，生活得有条有理。那样，一辈子都会愉快的。有条有理的生活，这多么好哇……”

老犀牛爷爷说完不久，就含笑离开了这个世界。在他咽气前的一刻，他还在轻轻地、高兴地念着：
“拖鞋、皮靴床底下，
窗台上面有牙刷。
……
用完东西别乱放，
请把它们送回家。”
full_text_en:
[P1] Ninety-nine years of worries and one year of happiness

[P2] Grandpa Rhinoceros lived for ninety-nine years.
He muddled through ninety-nine years.
He spent his whole life looking for things, looking for his own
things, looking for things he didn't know where he put them.

You know, Grandpa Rhinoceros, since he was a baby,
has had a bad memory. He spends every day
losing things and wasting a lot of time looking for them.

For example, when he goes to school — he doesn't know where his backpack is;
when he's in class — he searches his backpack but can't find his pencil;
when he goes home — he checks every pocket but can't find the key to open the door;
when he does homework at home — he finds out again
that his textbook is in the
classroom...

In short, he's very
confused!

062
063

[P3] Even when he got old, he was still like this. Every morning, he had to search for his shoes barefoot, then carry his teacup to look for his toothbrush, and after finding it, search for his toothpaste. Before he could even wash his face, he had already spent a full two hours.

Someone helped Grandpa Rhino calculate: in his 99 years, he spent 33 years sleeping—just like everyone else. The remaining 66 years, he probably spent

sixty years looking for things—his own things. Only six years were spent doing what he should have been doing.

This is not exaggerated at all. Grandpa Rhino himself admits he has been troubled by this his whole life. Perhaps you children have had this experience too: someone who is always looking for things can never be happy. Grandpa Rhino, because he spent so much time searching for things, became too nervous and ended up with heart disease and high blood pressure.

[P4] Just after Old Rhino Grandpa turned ninety-nine, a new neighbor moved in next door — a little raccoon.

The little raccoon was very clean. Old Rhino Grandpa met him by the stream, where the little raccoon often washed things — handkerchiefs, undershirts, and even food — he washed everything.

The raccoon's home was also extremely clean, spotless everywhere, with everything neatly arranged. There wasn't a single item out of place. The room was arranged just like a store's display window — looking both beautiful and comfortable.

[P5] Soon, little raccoon came to Old Rhino Grandpa's house for a visit.
As soon as he walked in, he jumped in surprise: it was just like a杂货仓库 (general store warehouse), with things scattered everywhere, and not even a place to put his feet. Old Rhino Grandpa wanted to pour tea for his guest, but couldn't find the teacup anywhere.

Little raccoon made up his mind to help Old Rhino Grandpa tidy up his house. He spent three whole days doing it, throwing out half of the useless things in the house, and washing every single item from the remaining half—washing so much that the stream water turned black.

[P6] Grandpa Rhinoceros couldn't recognize his own house anymore. It was so spacious and bright. He had only seen such a beautiful house when watching plays at the theater.

Grandpa Rhinoceros took off his boots and was about to crawl under the cupboard to look for his slippers when Little Raccoon said, "No! The slippers are under the bed." Grandpa Rhinoceros grabbed them for the first time without even looking. He was so happy, laughing with wrinkles appearing all over his face.

It was already very late. Grandpa Rhinoceros fell asleep on his clean and cozy bed.

[P7] The next morning, when he turned over and sat up,
he remembered the song the little raccoon taught him yesterday:
"Slippers and boots under the bed,
Toothbrush on the windowsill.
The basin is by the sink,
Flowered towel hanging in the corner.
Don't leave things messy after use,
Please return them home."

Usually, things that took two hours to finish,
were completed in ten minutes today. Grandpa Rhinoceros was amazed.

The morning air was so fresh. Grandpa Rhinoceros
wanted to go for a walk by the river. Usually, he didn't have time to walk in the morning. He wanted to crawl under the bed to find his shoes, hat, and coat. Suddenly, he remembered:
"Hanging behind the door, scarf and hat.
Hidden in the cabinet, clothes and coat.
Please go home and put them away just as you found them."

[P8] Five minutes later, Grandpa Rhinoceros was dressed and ready to go out. Walking by the little river, he greeted all the friends he met, and he felt wonderful. His friends were also very happy; they saw Grandpa Rhinoceros dressed neatly for the first time, out for an early morning walk.

Needless to say, from then on, Grandpa Rhinoceros's life became well-organized. He no longer had to spend all day looking for things, and his heart disease and high blood pressure were cured. He smiled all day long.

Unfortunately, just after his hundredth birthday, Grandpa Rhinoceros caught a severe cold and then developed pneumonia, and he became seriously ill. Grandpa Rhinoceros knew his illness couldn't be cured, because he was too old.

[P9] He told his visiting friends, "I am very happy. I lived to be a hundred, but I spent ninety-nine years in trouble. Thanks to little raccoon's help, I've lived this year so happily. I'm so happy! I hope everyone can be like me, not like little raccoon, living in an orderly way. That way, we'll all be happy for life. An orderly life—how wonderful it is..."

Soon after saying this, Old Rhino Grandpa passed away with a smile. At the moment he took his last breath, he was still softly and happily reciting:
"Slippers and boots under the bed,
Toothbrush on the windowsill.
...
Don't leave things lying around after use,
Please send them home."
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页展示了绘本的标题：‘九十九年烦恼和一年快乐’，文字竖排，无其他画面或对话内容。
[P2] 本页介绍了老犀牛爷爷因记性差而一辈子都在找东西的糊涂生活，并通过上学、上课、回家、做作业等具体例子说明他总是丢三落四，最后总结他是个糊涂蛋。
[P3] 本页通过具体描述老犀牛爷爷每天清晨找东西的糊涂生活，以及有人帮他算账的统计，说明他一生中大部分时间都在找东西，只有很少时间做正事，最终因长期紧张而患上心脏病和高血压。
[P4] 本页介绍了老犀牛爷爷的邻居小浣熊，他非常爱干净，常在溪边洗各种东西，而他的家也收拾得井井有条，像商店橱窗一样整洁漂亮。
[P5] 小浣熊来到老犀牛爷爷家做客，发现屋里乱七八糟，连茶杯都找不到。他决定帮忙整理，花了三天时间清理并清洗了所有物品，导致溪水都变黑了。
[P6] 老犀牛爷爷在小浣熊的帮助下整理好房子后，第一次轻松地找到了拖鞋，感到非常开心，并在干净整洁的床上安心入睡。
[P7] 老犀牛爷爷在小浣熊教的歌谣帮助下，迅速找到了所有物品，感到非常惊奇；随后他想散步时，又想起歌谣，自觉地将物品归位，展现了习惯养成后的改变。
[P8] 老犀牛爷爷在整理好生活后，心情愉快地出门散步，生活变得井然有序，疾病也痊愈了；但不幸的是，他在百岁生日后因重感冒和肺炎病倒，因年事已高而无法治愈。
[P9] 老犀牛爷爷在生命最后时刻向伙伴们分享了自己因生活有序而获得的快乐，并在临终前仍念着小浣熊教的整理歌谣，含笑离世。
[P10] 页面展示了一张整洁的床铺，配有床头柜、相框和窗台上的花瓶，床单为紫色条纹，整体环境干净有序，暗示老犀牛爷爷整理后的卧室。
